title: Police knew man was ill: Family: [Ontario Edition]
article: Police knew that a man who died after being pepper-sprayed in custody had ongoing problems with mental illness, his brother says.

"The police knew very well he was ill. I called them before many times and they have explained they need a document to pick him up under the Mental Health Act. They picked him up under the Mental Health Act once before," Demetrius Blentzas said last night.

Toronto police went to Nicholas Blentzas' apartment building on Thorncliffe Park Dr. shortly after midnight Sunday to answer a disturbance call. Demetrius said he and his mother were not home when Nicholas arrived. He had a panic attack because he lost his keys and began smashing at the apartment door with a fire extinguisher.
Police tried to subdue Nicholas and used pepper spray in an effort to control him. He collapsed a short time later and was dead on arrival at Toronto East General Hospital.
Demetrius said Nicholas, 24, suffered from a bipolar disorder and was taking lithium to control his outbursts, but was not a violent person.

He said he couldn't understand how it happened that his brother calmly left the 17th floor hallway with two officers, went down the elevator and walked across the street to their cruiser where something occurred requiring police to use pepper spray.
Demetrius said police were there the previous night when he called because his brother became agitated. Two officers arrived but could not remove Nicholas because they lacked a doctor's form.

The special investigations unit, which probes cases of serious injury or death involving police, has named five subject officers in the case, spokesperson Rose Hong said. Six SIU investigators canvassed residents for information about police contact with Nicholas.

Hong said results of an autopsy yesterday are being withheld because officials still haven't interviewed some witnesses. "We don't want to be tainting witness statements and affecting the integrity of what we're doing."
